parsed.explanation: No general criminalisation of trans identity and no sodomy law, so this is not a 0.05–0.15 state. But the combined regime imposes traveller-facing universal exposures: federal screening now scrutinises sex-marker discrepancies with refusal and possible lifetime misrepresentation findings, federal facilities are barred from identity-congruent use, and this division mandates birth-sex access to all public facilities, shelters, and prison placement. It additionally carries surviving criminal statutes (impersonation/adult-performance, an indecent-exposure definition aimed at congruent bathroom use) and documented severe abuse of trans people in immigration custody. Recourse is thin: gender identity is absent from the state hate-crime statute, a panic defence survives, and border remedies are uncertain. That places it below denial-of-entry-but-no-custody anchors and well above imprisonment-for-status anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal case-note tagging and refusal where documents cast doubt on sex; suspected misrepresentation can support a permanent inadmissibility finding; X markers no longer issued; allied governments issued advisories and reported detentions over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Misrepresentation findings require all four elements and are never automatic; limited waiver possibilities; passport-marker rule remains in litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport with a marker or name mismatching presentation moves the traveller from routine entry into tagged secondary adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections policies impose birth-sex grooming and hormone removal on inmates; this division mandates prison placement by birth sex.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; a legal-aid FAQ exists on document rules. No working custody remedy is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document discrepancy can escalate into detention and then birth-sex placement, moving the traveller between federal and state custodial systems.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from identity-congruent single-sex federal facilities; this division requires birth-sex use of all public facilities and bars trans women from women's shelters; a 2019 statute frames congruent bathroom use as indecent exposure.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The 2021 warning-sign requirement was struck down; one state's trespass statute requires willful entry plus refusal to depart. Neither protects access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Restroom, shelter or hospital-ward access is set by birth sex at both levels, an unavoidable exposure for an outed traveller.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned for minors, with civil penalties for adults who help a minor obtain it and out-of-state telehealth reach; care banned for inmates. Adult visitor care itself is not documented as denied.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor cannot access care here, and adults assisting one face civil exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The only state with a surviving criminal ban on gender-expressive performance (impersonators where a child could see), up to ~1 year first offence, felony on repeat; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; a 2026 safety act frames trans women as a facility threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism guidance states powers will not target mere disagreement; no prosecution of a trans person under the performance law is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Public presentation at events or near children can be reframed from expression into a criminal or security matter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban with regret suits against parents and $25,000 actions by the chief prosecutor; schools must out gender-nonconforming students; teachers shielded for birth-certificate pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: School-outing directive was preliminarily enjoined in 2022; several federal orders are blocked in court.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces aid-and-abetment exposure; school rules reach only residents.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Recorded killings of trans women at 7.8 per 100k/yr, described as an undercount floor; gay/trans panic defence available; 2021 reporting of officials ignoring anti-LGBTQ assaults; hate-crime statute omits gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A 2019 chief-prosecutor opinion treats anti-trans victim selection as gender bias for sentencing; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police discretion plus a panic defence weakens deterrence and reporting for a victim-stranger.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement of the indecent-exposure definition, the prison-care ban and the 2026 facility provisions is unsourced; state licence-marker litigation outcome unknown; multiple federal measures enjoined or pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment ruling and hate-crimes statute provide partial recourse; municipal ordinances cover public employment only and are preempted as to private employers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether a traveller could obtain relief after a facility or performance charge is unresolved in the record.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A mandates severe multi-year imprisonment for identity misrepresentation with consular access denied. Here no statute criminalises trans status itself and entry refusal, not imprisonment, is the standard border outcome, so this case sits materially higher.

0.25-A involves invasive review, document confiscation and denial of entry but no facility-by-birth-sex mandate, no criminal impersonation statute and no documented custodial abuse. This jurisdiction adds those tier-1 and tier-2 layers, so it scores slightly below.

0.35-A is stopped by an enforceable charter prohibiting prolonged holds for document discrepancies and releases the traveller without detention. Here no comparable operating border protection exists and facilities and custody are birth-sex mandated, so this case sits below that anchor.

0.55-B has a functioning non-discrimination code, staff correcting records respectfully and no custody or facility exposure. Nothing equivalent is documented here, so this jurisdiction is substantially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a layered one: federal screening treats a sex-marker or name discrepancy as a possible material misrepresentation, and refusal plus a permanent finding is a real, documented outcome; state law then mandates birth-sex access to every public facility and shelter and birth-sex prison placement, and keeps a criminal impersonation statute and an indecent-exposure definition touching bathroom use. For an outed traveller these are continuous, inescapable exposures that no local tolerance offsets. Recourse is weak — no gender-identity hate-crime coverage, a surviving panic defence, and an unremedied custodial record — though no statute criminalises trans status itself and litigation has blocked several federal measures, keeping the case above the imprisonment-for-status tier.
